records.label: ADCME pedigree
records.onset: between the ages of 12 and 50 years

phenotypes.text: mild mental retardation in patients with intractable seizures
frontotemporal and generalized interictal EEG abnormalities
cortical origin of myoclonus with EEG-EMG coherence

records.segregation: linked to 2p11.1-q12.2, max two-point LOD 3.46 at D2S2175
quotes: We describe a pedigree in which eight individuals presented with a non-progressive disorder with onset between the ages of 12 and 50 years. It was characterized by predominantly distal, semi-continuous rhythmic myoclonus (all patients), generalized tonic-clonic seizures (all patients) and complex partial seizures (three patients).
Most individuals had rarely suffered seizures and had a normal cognitive level, but three individuals with intractable seizures had mild mental retardation.
All patients had frontotemporal as well as generalized interictal EEG abnormalities.

records.label: Four-generation European FAME kindred

phenotypes.hpo_label: Bilateral tonic-clonic seizure with generalized onset

records.segregation: Linkage to the FAME/BAFME locus on 8q23.3-q24.1 was excluded
quotes: Ten living and three deceased relatives had the clinical characteristics of FAME. Mean age at onset of the 10 living patients was 41 years (range, 30-60 years). Eight of the 13 affected subjects had generalized tonic-clonic seizures.

Electrophysiologic studies confirmed the diagnosis of FAME in the five patients studied. The pattern of inheritance was consistent with an autosomal dominant inheritance. The locus responsible for FAME/BAFME was excluded.

records.label: Two Italian BAFME families
quotes: The authors report a clinical and electrophysiologic study of two Italian BAFME families showing linkage to chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2.

records.label: Five-generation family from Naples
records.segregation: Significant linkage to chromosome 2p (maximum lod score 5.9)
quotes: We report a five-generation family showing cortical tremor, myoclonus, and epilepsy, originating from Naples, Italy. Eleven members, aged 24-56 years (mean: 39.2 years), suffered from hand tremor and myoclonus, whereas generalized seizures occurred in six.

In addition, giant somatosensory-evoked potential components and enhanced long loop reflex I were found also in three presymptomatic members who manifested hand tremor and myoclonus at upper limbs after 1.5 years of follow-up.

records.label: Five southern Italian BAFME families
records.segregation: Haplotype 5332 at D2S388, D2S2216, D2S113, D2S2175 segregated with disease in all families; maximum cumulative lod 18.5
quotes: Five Italian BAFME families were identified. One family has not been previously reported. DNA from 53 affected individuals was genotyped
The haplotype "5332" of adjacent markers D2S388, D2S2216, D2S113, and D2S2175 segregates with the disease in all families

records.label: Italian FCMTE family
records.segregation: Affected members shared a common 14.5-Mb haplotype in the pericentromeric region of chromosome 2; 8q24 excluded
quotes: Clinically affected members of the family had limb and voice tremor, seizures, and myoclonus involving the eyelids during blinking.
Neuropsychological testing disclosed visuospatial impairment, possibly due to temporal lobe dysfunction.
Linkage analysis excluded the 8q24 locus, where patients shared a common haplotype spanning 14.5 Mb in the pericentromeric region of chromosome 2.

records.label: 6-generation FAME kindred
records.ancestry: European descent; New Zealand and Australia
records.onset: hand tremor median age 15 years (range 4-60 years)

phenotypes.text: cortical reflex myoclonus on neurophysiological testing

quotes: A 6-generation FAME kindred of European descent was ascertained in New Zealand and Australia. Affected family members (N = 55) had fine hand tremor, with onset typically in adolescence (median age, 15 years; age range, 4-60 years).

Proximal myoclonus was present in 44 of 55 (80%), arising later than hand tremor (median age, 17 years; age range, 5-60 years). Generalized tonic-clonic seizures occurred in 8 of 55 (15%), with a median age at onset of 43.5 years (age range, 18-76 years).
Neurophysiological testing confirmed features of cortical reflex myoclonus.

notes.statement: Corbett et al. (2019) used whole-genome sequencing with ExpansionHunter and exSTRa in affected members of 3 FAME families and identified an expansion of the endogenous ATTTT repeat with an inserted ATTTC repeat in the first intron of STARD7 within the FAME2 interval on chromosome 2. The ATTTC repeat was absent from WGS data of 69 controls.
quotes: This revealed an expansion of an ATTTT repeat and insertion of an ATTTC repeat in the context of the reverse strand of chr2 within the first intron of STARD7 (StAR-related lipid transfer domain-containing 7) in all FAME samples tested
The ATTTC repeat was not present in any whole-genome sequencing data from 69 control samples

notes.statement: Corbett et al. (2019) found by repeat-primed PCR that the ATTTC expansion segregated in 158/158 affected individuals from 22 FAME pedigrees; 2 of 24 tested individuals without a FAME diagnosis carried the expansion and were likely presymptomatic. The expansion was not amplified in 28 control DNA samples.
quotes: The ATTTC expansions segregate in 158/158 individuals typically affected by FAME from 22 pedigrees including 16 previously reported families recruited worldwide.
Of the 24 individuals tested in these families that did not have a FAME diagnosis, two were positive for the ATTTC expansion; both were from younger generations and likely presymptomatic.
The ATTTC repeat expansion did not amplify in any of 28 control DNA samples extracted from unaffected individuals unrelated to FAME.

notes.statement: Corbett et al. (2019) screened 52 unrelated patients with generalized epilepsy and tremor or adult-onset myoclonic epilepsy and found the STARD7 ATTTC expansion in only 1. Among family members with uncertain FAME diagnosis, usually tremor alone, 8 of 13 carried the expansion.
quotes: Of these, 20/20 familial and 1/52 singleton cases were positive for an ATTTC expansion in STARD7

Finally, within the families we tested, there were 13 individuals where the diagnosis of FAME was uncertain, usually due to a history of tremor with no other diagnostic features. Of these, 8/13 carried the ATTTC expansion.

notes.statement: Corbett et al. (2019) determined by long-read sequencing that the pathogenic allele had the structure (AAATG)n(AAAAT)n. In one patient, a SMRT read contained 274 AAATG and 387 AAAAT repeats while a nanopore read contained 345 AAATG and 390 AAAAT repeats, suggesting somatic variation in repeat size. Another patient's allele was 4,645 bp long.
quotes: The SMRT read generated to 99% base accuracy by circular consensus calling was comprised of four subreads and contained 274 AAATG and 387 AAAAT repeats, without interruption from other sequences.
The Oxford Nanopore read contained 345 AAATG and 390 AAAAT repeats with some interruptions, suggesting somatic variation of repeat sizes may occur within the one individual.

notes.statement: Corbett et al. (2019) found the STARD7 ATTTC expansion in 2 families that carried the previously reported ADRA2B variant. They concluded that this strongly suggested the ADRA2B allele is not causative.
quotes: This included two families with the previously identified ADRA2B; c.675_686delTGGTGGGGCTTTinsGTTTGGCAG; p.H225_L229delinsQ225_F_G_R228 variant strongly suggesting that allele is not causative (Table 1; Family 4 & 15).

notes.statement: Corbett et al. (2019) found evidence of anticipation in a large Australian/New Zealand FAME2 family. Median age at onset was 30 years in generation III, 17 years in generation IV, and 12 years in generation V.
quotes: We found evidence of anticipation; generation III had a median onset of 30 years (range 14–60 y, n = 6), in generation IV median onset was 17 years (8–50 y, n = 30) and the median onset in generation V was 12 years (4–19 y, n = 16).

notes.statement: Corbett et al. (2019) found that STARD7 transcript and protein levels were not altered in patient-derived fibroblasts. No RNA-seq reads containing ATTTC repeats were detected. They suggested that the repeat sequence alone is pathogenic, independent of any effect on the host gene.
quotes: Reads containing ATTTC repeats were not present in the RNA-Seq data despite robust expression of STARD7.
These data suggest the repeat sequence alone is pathogenic, independent of an effect on the coding sequence of the encompassing gene.

notes.statement: Corbett et al. (2019) reported that a repeat-primed PCR assay for the ATTTC repeat was diagnostic for FAME, with 100% sensitivity in families linked or suggestively linked to chromosome 2. They noted that FAME2 is the most frequently linked locus in Caucasian patients.
quotes: however, the ATTTC repeat primer was diagnostic for FAME with a sensitivity of 100% in all families with linkage or suggestive linkage to chr2.
The FAME2 locus is the most frequently observed linked region for Caucasian individuals affected by this disorder whereas chromosome 8 thus far is limited to Asian individuals

notes.statement: Corbett et al. (2019) noted that increased cerebellar choline on proton MR spectroscopy had previously been found in 11 individuals from 3 Italian families, all of which they showed to carry the ATTTC expansion. Because STARD7 transfers phosphatidylcholine, they suggested this finding may be peculiar to FAME2.
quotes: Previously, increased levels of choline have been detected by proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS) in the cerebellum of 11 individuals from three Italian families all shown here to have the ATTTC dynamic mutation (Table 1).

notes.statement: In a 5-generation Tuscan family with autosomal dominant cortical myoclonus and epilepsy (ADCME) previously mapped to chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2, De Fusco et al. (2014) identified an in-frame insertion/deletion in the ADRA2B gene (c.675_686delTGGTGGGGCTTTinsGTTTGGCAG; p.His225_Leu229delinsGlnPheGlyArg) that replaced 5 amino acids (HGGAL) with 4 new ones (QFGR). It segregated completely with the disease and was not found in 575 Tuscan controls or in public databases. Next-generation sequencing of the critical region in 2 affected members found no other relevant change.
quotes: we identified a novel in-frame insertion/deletion in the α2-adrenergic receptor subtype B gene (α2B-AR; ADRA2B), which substitutes five amino acids, HGGAL, with four new residues, QFGR,
This indel mutation completely co-segregates with the disease phenotype and is absent in 575 unrelated controls from Tuscany
The ADRA2B mutation was confirmed as the unique relevant chance (data not shown).

notes.statement: De Fusco et al. (2014) found the same ADRA2B indel in a second Tuscan ADCME family. The 2 families had no known kinship but shared the same disease haplotype across the entire critical region, which suggested a common ancestor.
quotes: Although no kinship between the two families was discovered by anamnestic analysis of members of the two pedigrees, a common ancestor is to be expected as they share the same disease haplotype spanning the entire critical region on chromosome 2

notes.statement: De Fusco et al. (2014) found no ADRA2B mutations in BAFME pedigrees from southern Italy that mapped to the ADCME locus. They also excluded large insertions or deletions by Southern blot. The authors suggested that ADCME and BAFME/FAME might be distinct clinical entities, but they could not exclude variants in noncoding regulatory regions.
quotes: BAFME pedigrees originating from Southern Italy have been shown to map in the ADCME locus. However, we failed to detect any ADRA2B mutations in these pedigrees by direct sequence analysis and excluded potential large insertion and deletions by southern blot
suggesting the possibility of classifying ADCME and BAFME/FAME as two distinct clinical entities

notes.statement: De Fusco et al. (2014) found no evidence of cardiovascular disease in any of the ADCME patients, despite ADRA2B expression in heart and vascular smooth muscle. Two of the oldest ADRA2B mutation carriers developed age-related dementia.
quotes: A careful anamnesis was performed on all ADCME patients giving negative evidence for cardiovascular diseases; two of the oldest ADRA2B mutation carriers developed age-related dementia.

notes.statement: In transfected HeLa cells, De Fusco et al. (2014) found that mutant alpha-2B-AR localized normally to the plasma membrane and was internalized in an arrestin-3-dependent manner, like wildtype. In coimmunoprecipitation studies, however, the mutant receptor failed to form a stable complex with spinophilin: spinophilin binding to the mutant fell back to baseline after 10 minutes of epinephrine stimulation, whereas binding to wildtype remained elevated.
quotes: These results suggest that both wild type and mutant α2B-AR internalize in an arrestin-3-dependent manner

However, the amount of spinophilin co-isolated with the mutant α2B-AR dropped back to the basal level after epinephrine treatment for 10 min, whereas the amount of spinophilin co-isolated with the wild type α2B-AR remained elevated with the same treatment (Fig. 5C).

notes.statement: In Xenopus oocytes, spinophilin increased the EC50 for epinephrine-stimulated calcium signaling through wildtype alpha-2B-AR but not through the mutant receptor. De Fusco et al. (2014) concluded that the mutation increases the intensity of Ca2+ signaling, a gain-of-function effect caused by loss of the spinophilin interaction. They proposed that the resulting cortical hyperexcitability might stem from impaired GABAergic inhibition.
quotes: The expression of the mutant α2B-AR exhibits per se a trend toward significant reduction of the EC50 compared to wild type (p=0.055), but the presence of spinophilin does not result in an increase in EC50
We propose that the ADCME mutation exerts a gain of function effect by reducing the interaction with spinophilin, and thus increasing receptor activity.
Thus, cortical hyperexcitability in ADCME might result from impaired GABAergic inhibition

notes.statement: De Fusco et al. (2014) described ADCME as familial cortical reflex myoclonus: an action-induced shivering movement of the hands and upper-limb jerking, variably associated with focal and generalized tonic-clonic seizures. A minority of patients had borderline or moderately impaired cognition, and myoclonus often worsened in advanced age.
quotes: ADCME is characterized by familial occurrence of cortical reflex myoclonus manifested as action-induced shivering movement of the hands and upper limb jerking variably associated with focal and generalized tonic-clonic seizures of variable severity and, in a minority of patients, with borderline or moderately impaired cognitive skills.

notes.statement: Crompton et al. (2012) narrowed the FAME2 locus on chromosome 2 to a 13.3-Mb interval containing 99 known protein-coding genes, using genetic mapping in a large 6-generation family.
quotes: Genetic mapping narrows the FAME2 (OMIM 607876) locus on chromosome 2 to a 13.3-megabase interval, harboring 99 known protein-coding genes.

notes.statement: Crompton et al. (2012) found that the most common FAME phenotype in a large family was a mild postural hand tremor resembling essential tremor, combined with subtle proximal myoclonus. Generalized tonic-clonic seizures were uncommon and occurred around sleep onset following severe generalized myoclonus.
quotes: The most common FAME phenotype in this large family is mild postural hand tremor resembling essential tremor, combined with subtle proximal myoclonus. Generalized tonic-clonic seizures are uncommon and occur around sleep onset following severe generalized myoclonus.

notes.statement: In an Italian family with familial cortical myoclonic tremor with epilepsy, Suppa et al. (2009) excluded linkage to the 8q24 locus. Affected members shared a common haplotype spanning 14.5 Mb in the pericentromeric region of chromosome 2.
quotes: Linkage analysis excluded the 8q24 locus, where patients shared a common haplotype spanning 14.5 Mb in the pericentromeric region of chromosome 2.

notes.statement: Suppa et al. (2009) found that neurophysiologic findings in affected family members suggested increased excitability of the primary motor cortex with normal sensorimotor integration. On neuropsychological testing, patients had visuospatial impairment, which the authors suggested was possibly due to temporal lobe dysfunction.
quotes: Neurophysiologic findings suggested increased primary motor cortex excitability with normal sensorimotor integration.
Neuropsychological testing disclosed visuospatial impairment, possibly due to temporal lobe dysfunction.

notes.statement: Madia et al. (2008) found significant linkage of BAFME to chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2 in 5 southern Italian families, with a maximum cumulative lod score of 18.5 for markers D2S2161 and D2S388.
quotes: Significant linkage was found on chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2 and a maximum cumulative lod score of 18.5 was found for markers D2S2161 and D2S388.

notes.statement: Madia et al. (2008) found that a haplotype ('5332') of adjacent markers D2S388, D2S2216, D2S113, and D2S2175 segregated with the disease in all 5 Italian families, indicating that the same mutation inherited from a common ancestor segregated in these families.
quotes: The haplotype "5332" of adjacent markers D2S388, D2S2216, D2S113, and D2S2175 segregates with the disease in all families indicating that the same mutation inherited from a common ancestor segregates in these families.

notes.statement: Madia et al. (2008) found in preliminary analyses that patients carrying the disease haplotype showed minor clinical differences, suggesting that expressivity of the founder mutation is not markedly influenced by other factors.
quotes: Preliminary genotype-phenotype showed that patients carrying the disease haplotype show minor clinical differences, suggesting that expressivity of the founder mutation is not markedly influenced by other factors.

notes.statement: Saint-Martin et al. (2008) refined the 2p11.1-q12.2 locus responsible for cortical tremor associated with epilepsy and excluded candidate genes in the region.
quotes: Refinement of the 2p11.1-q12.2 locus responsible for cortical tremor associated with epilepsy and exclusion of candidate genes.

notes.statement: Striano et al. (2005) found significant linkage to chromosome 2p (maximum lod score of 5.9) in a 5-generation Italian family with cortical tremor, myoclonus, and epilepsy.
quotes: Genetic study of the pedigree revealed a significant linkage on chromosome 2p (maximum lod score = 5.9).

notes.statement: Striano et al. (2005) found cortical reflex myoclonus on electrophysiologic study in all affected family members. Three presymptomatic members had giant somatosensory-evoked potential components and an enhanced long loop reflex I, and all 3 developed hand tremor and upper-limb myoclonus after 1.5 years of follow-up.
quotes: Electrophysiological study confirmed the presence of cortical reflex myoclonus in all affected members.

In addition, giant somatosensory-evoked potential components and enhanced long loop reflex I were found also in three presymptomatic members who manifested hand tremor and myoclonus at upper limbs after 1.5 years of follow-up.

notes.statement: de Falco et al. (2003) found linkage to chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2 in 2 Italian families with benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy (BAFME).
quotes: The authors report a clinical and electrophysiologic study of two Italian BAFME families showing linkage to chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2.

notes.statement: de Falco et al. (2003) noted that BAFME had been mapped to chromosome 8q24 and that their findings in Italian families supported genetic heterogeneity and suggested possible allelism with autosomal dominant cortical myoclonus and epilepsy (ADCME).
quotes: Benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy (BAFME) has been mapped to chromosome 8q24; however, genetic heterogeneity has been recently suggested.
suggests a possible allelism with the recently described autosomal dominant cortical myoclonus and epilepsy syndrome.

notes.statement: Labauge et al. (2002) excluded linkage to the FAME/BAFME locus on 8q23.3-q24.1 in a 4-generation European family with familial adult myoclonic epilepsy. They concluded that this showed the disorder is genetically heterogeneous, and that the family extended the occurrence of FAME to non-Japanese patients.
quotes: Exclusion of linkage of this family to the locus for familial adult myoclonic epilepsy/benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy established the genetic heterogeneity of this disorder.
Observation of a European family extends the occurrence of familial adult myoclonic epilepsy to non-Japanese patients.

notes.statement: Guerrini et al. (2001) performed genome-wide linkage analysis in the ADCME family and identified a 12.4-cM critical region between D2S2161 and D2S1897 on 2p11.1-q12.2, with a maximum two-point LOD score of 3.46 at theta = 0.0 for D2S2175 and a multipoint LOD of 3.74 around D2S2175.
quotes: Genome-wide linkage analysis identified a critical region spanning 12.4 cM between markers D2S2161 and D2S1897 in 2p11.1-q12.2, with a maximum two-point LOD score of 3.46 at Theta 0.0 for marker D2S2175.
Multipoint LOD score values, reaching 3.74 around D2S2175, localize the ADCME gene to the centromeric region of chromosome 2.

notes.statement: Guerrini et al. (2001) excluded linkage to the familial adult myoclonic epilepsy locus on chromosome 8q23.3-q24 in their family and concluded that the 2cen localization and different phenotype defined a new epilepsy syndrome.
quotes: The exclusion of the locus for familial adult myoclonic epilepsy on chromosome 8q23.3-q24 from linkage to our family and the new localization of the responsible gene to chromosome 2cen, together with the different phenotype, define a new epilepsy syndrome.

notes.statement: Guerrini et al. (2001) found that the pattern of inheritance of ADCME was autosomal dominant with high penetrance.
quotes: The pattern of inheritance was autosomal dominant with high penetrance.

notes.statement: Guerrini et al. (2001) found that the resting motor threshold to transcranial magnetic stimulation was significantly reduced and the post-MEP silent period significantly shortened (101 vs 137 ms in controls) in patients. EEG-EMG coherence at 8-25 Hz over the contralateral rolandic area in 5 patients, with EEG preceding EMG by 8-15 ms, suggested a cortical origin of the myoclonus, and ipsilateral coherence in 2 suggested transcallosal spread. The authors suggested diffuse cortical hyperexcitability particularly involving frontotemporal circuits.
quotes: The resting motor threshold intensity to transcranial magnetic stimulation was significantly reduced (38%; SD +/- 7; P = 0.01) and the post-motor evoked potential silent period (101 ms; SEM +/- 10) was significantly shortened compared with the controls (137 ms; SEM +/- 18).

The frequency of coherence was 8-25 Hz and phase spectra confirmed that EEG activity preceded EMG activity by 8-15 ms. In two individuals there was also significant coherence between the ipsilateral EEG and EMG, consistent with the transcallosal spread of myoclonic activity.
We hypothesize that the responsible gene causes cortical hyperexcitability that is widespread but particularly involves the frontotemporal circuits.
